cases.label: USA, January 1974 — year-round emergency DST
cases.note: The Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act put the US on DST through the winter of 1973-74, so this January reading is EDT (-04), not EST.

cases.label: Indiana, June 2004 — before statewide DST
cases.note: Indiana largely stayed on EST year-round until 2006, so June 2004 is -05.

cases.label: Indiana, June 2007 — after statewide DST
cases.note: From 2006 Indiana observes DST, so the same June reading is -04.

cases.label: Israel, July 1993 — annually legislated DST
cases.note: Israeli DST dates were set by annual legislation through the 1990s rather than by a standing rule; tzdata carries each year separately.

cases.label: Netherlands, 1930 — Amsterdam time
cases.note: Europe/Amsterdam ran on +00:19:32 from 1835 to 1937, plus Dutch summer time in June 1930, giving +01:19:32. A sub-minute offset most engines round away.

cases.label: Arizona, July — no DST
cases.note: Arizona does not observe DST, so July is -07 while its neighbours are -06.

cases.label: Navajo Nation, July — observes DST
cases.note: The Navajo Nation does observe DST; tzdata models it as America/Denver (America/Shiprock is a link to that zone), so the same July reading is -06.

cases.label: Sydney, October — southern-hemisphere DST
cases.note: DST starts in October in the southern hemisphere, giving +11.

cases.label: US spring-forward 2024 — 02:30 does not exist
cases.note: 02:30 falls in the gap; §5 requires shifting forward by the gap length.

cases.label: US fall-back 2024 — 01:30 occurs twice
cases.note: 01:30 occurs twice; §5 requires taking the earlier offset.
